name: Set a small part on the surface grinder's magnetic chuck, blocked in by steel keepers, and switch the chuck on

working.role: wipes the chuck, sets the keepers and the part, turns the chuck's lever

steadying.role: holds each keeper or the part down against the one being set while the working hand pushes it tight

phases.what: The chuck off (the lever pointing right), the wheel stopped and raised clear [proposed: duration_s]
Wipe the chuck's face clean where the work will sit, and the part's and the keepers' undersides: a chip under them lifts them off the poles [proposed: force_n, duration_s]
phases.ends_on: no chips or grit on the face

phases.what: Lay the first keeper flat on the chuck, square to the table's travel by eye [proposed: duration_s]
phases.ends_on: the keeper flat, square by eye

phases.what: Set the part on the chuck, its face to be ground up, one flank against the first keeper [proposed: duration_s]

Each further keeper laid flat against the next flank and slid in until it touches, the steadying hand holding the part down against the keepers already set; keepers placed so none crosses another or runs off the chuck [proposed: force_n, duration_s]
The working hand to the chuck's lever
Lever half a turn to on, the steadying hand off the work [proposed: duration_s]
phases.ends_on: the lever at its far stop

phases.what: Try the part and each keeper with a fingertip: the keepers don't move; the part is held, a light nudge only, as a hard sideways knock wedges a clearance-ground insert up over its keepers [proposed: force_n, duration_s]

sources.ref: South Bend Lathe Co., Model SB1029 Owner's Manual (2010): Magnetic Chuck and Setup for a Typical Grinding Operation (p. 31: both faces ground flat and clean, the chuck off to place the work, then on), Operation Overview (p. 20: the head raised clear, the table wiped)
sources.gives: clean faces, the chuck off to place the work and on to hold it

sources.ref: The station's magnetic chuck (moonshot/library/stations/sgrind.json chuck; moonshot/world/sgrind.py): carbide holds at about 6% of steel's pull (its cobalt binder), so a carbide part is blocked in by steel keepers the magnet holds (your decision, 2026-11-06); and the grinder cell's tests (moonshot/tests/test_grind_cell.py)
sources.gives: why keepers, how tight (0.05 mm off each flank), that they lie in a pinwheel so none crosses another, and that a 1 N nudge leaves the part in its pocket while a sideways knock of about 6.5 N lifts an 11 deg clearance insert out

sources.ref: Tormach PSG 612 Operator's Manual UM10159: Using the Magnetic Chuck (p. 12)
sources.gives: the chuck switched on by its handle once the work is placed

sources.ref: Kurt, 'Double Station Manual Vise Setup' (YouTube), measured locally with MediaPipe Hand Landmarker; borrowed for reach durations
sources.gives: reach durations: the right hand's interquartile range, 0.32-0.67 s

notes: For a part too weakly magnetic, or too small, for the chuck to hold alone; a steel part thick enough is set straight on the chuck and phases 3 and 5 drop out. ct-tpg322's plan names the shop's 1/8 in parallels as keepers; laid round a triangle with a flank along the table's travel, 6 in keepers reach 256 mm across the 254 mm chuck and over 120 mm behind the insert, into the spindle housing's path with the 6 in wheel at the work, so the keepers' length is open with the coordinator (the cell takes any length). No footage of a grinder setup is measured yet. Proposed, with reasons (phase numbers count from 1): #1 1 s to check; #2 5 N and 3-6 s for a rag over a small area; #3 and #4 1.5 s each to lay a keeper or the part; #5 1 N, a fingertip's push that closes a 0.05 mm gap without shifting what is set, and 2-4 s a keeper; #7 the lever as the station's; #8 1 N, from the cell's tests, and 1.0 s.
